title: Best Full Marathons in Thailand
intro: Thailand's full marathons run from big-city road races in Bangkok and Chiang Mai out to provincial events in Nakhon Ratchasima, Khon Kaen and Songkhla that most visitors never hear about. The calendar leans heavily on the November-to-February window, when the northeast monsoon has passed and mornings are genuinely cool by regional standards. Fields vary enormously in size, and several of these are AIMS-certified courses, which matters if you're chasing a qualifying time rather than a weekend away.

faqs.question: When is marathon season in Thailand?
faqs.answer: The bulk of Thai marathons fall between November and February. That window sits after the rainy season and delivers the coolest mornings of the year, particularly in the north and northeast. Races outside it are far fewer and typically start earlier in the morning to compensate for heat.

faqs.question: Are Thai marathons suitable for a first-time marathoner?
faqs.answer: Many are, though heat is the deciding factor rather than terrain. Northern and northeastern courses in the cool season are the most forgiving. Check the flag-off time: a 4am start is common and changes how you would plan sleep, travel and the night before entirely.

editorial_pick: Our top pick is the Buriram Marathon (87/100), run on the Chang International Circuit -- an FIA Grade 1 motorsport track that's hosted MotoGP's Thai Grand Prix since 2018, a genuinely unusual course among Thailand's city and temple races.
